engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0 of 0.375 (minor)failThe requirement is that browser-driving tests wait for observable state before asserting and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by running the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser automation sleeps for a fixed time before collecting the state the tests assert on. In scripts/verify.mjs, renderEveryStep waits for the step index and then calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS), a fixed 1800 ms. Only after that does it read the title, caption and errors that the E2E test asserts on (the outline/render pass, &#39;VERIFY FAILED [outline] (step 1)&#39;, and the late-fault step attribution). The bootstrap inspect helper that tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs calls page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before collecting the diagnostics and screenshot behind each asserted warning. The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. So the &#39;no fixed sleeps / wait for observable state&#39; clause is unmet. This rules with Judge C. Judge A is right that the test files themselves contain no sleep calls and that the scripts poll data-step-index. That does not decide the requirement: the scripts are the browser-driving code these tests execute, they add a fixed sleep after that poll before the asserted state is read, and the integration test checks that this sleep happened. Judge B&#39;s evidence covers jsdom component tests (sample.test.tsx, presentation.test.tsx, router.test.tsx), which use waitFor/findBy and do not drive a browser. It also cites the spawnSync-based E2E test without looking at the fixed waitForTimeout inside the verify run that test drives. The keys differ, so React unmounts the wrapped instance and mounts a new one. The old instance plays its 0.6s exit while the new one mounts with the same layoutId. Before rendering, verify() checks only the hard-coded REFERENCE (validateReference) and a regex for the slug in the registry (checkRegistered). Because no step-0 runtime error is recorded, waitForSelector(&#39;[data-step-count]&#39;, 15_000) times out. That is the render-timeout path the guidance rules out, not a sample or outline check. This scenario comes straight from the guidance&#39;s definition of a missing sample. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by running the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser automation sleeps for a fixed time before collecting the state the tests assert on. In scripts/verify.mjs, renderEveryStep waits for the step index and then calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS), a fixed 1800 ms. Only after that does it read the title, caption and errors that the E2E test asserts on (the outline/render pass, &#39;VERIFY FAILED [outline] (step 1)&#39;, and the late-fault step attribution). The bootstrap inspect helper that tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs calls page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before collecting the diagnostics and screenshot behind each asserted warning. The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. So the &#39;no fixed sleeps / wait for observable state&#39; clause is unmet. This rules with Judge C. Judge A is right that the test files themselves contain no sleep calls and that the scripts poll data-step-index. That does not decide the requirement: the scripts are the browser-driving code these tests execute, they add a fixed sleep after that poll before the asserted state is read, and the integration test checks that this sleep happened. Judge B&#39;s evidence covers jsdom component tests (sample.test.tsx, presentation.test.tsx, router.test.tsx), which use waitFor/findBy and do not drive a browser. It also cites the spawnSync-based E2E test without looking at the fixed waitForTimeout inside the verify run that test drives. The quoted lines show this clause is not met. - **The tests drive the browser through scripts.** tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts runs scripts/verify.mjs, and tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs the bootstrap inspect-presentation.mjs. Those scripts do the browser automation. - **The scripts sleep for a fixed time.** Both scripts first poll data-step-index. Then they call page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS = 1800) or page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before reading the title, caption, errors, diagnostics and screenshot that the tests assert on. That is a fixed-millisecond wait for a transition, used in place of waiting on a settled state. - **The integration test depends on the sleep.** Lines 53-58 assert that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, so the test only passes if the fixed sleep happens. - **No other criterion covers this.** No other engineering-quality criterion names this defect, so scoring it here does not count it twice. - **The noise rule does not apply.** That rule only says no credit is given, and no fail is given, for missing *longer* settle delays. It does not excuse having fixed sleeps. The test files contain no sleep calls of their own, and the scripts do poll the step index. Neither point helps, because the requirement forbids any fixed sleep in the browser-driving path that the tests run and assert on.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs:17 sets SETTLE_MS = 1800. Those results are read only after the fixed 1800 ms sleep."],"citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts","tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts"],"marker":"","scope_repair":[],"criterion":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","cycle":"initial","part":0}],"contradiction_checks":[],"settlement":{"engineering-tests-wait-on-state":{"cycles":[{"cycle":"initial","expected_parts":[0]}],"settled_cycle":"initial"}},"audit_attempts":[{"stage":"tiebreak-span-audit","cycle":"initial","attempt":1,"ok":true,"error":null}],"decisions":[{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","vote":"fail","result":{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The requirement is that browser-driving tests wait for observable state before asserting and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by running the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser automation sleeps for a fixed time before collecting the state the tests assert on. In scripts/verify.mjs, renderEveryStep waits for the step index and then calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS), a fixed 1800 ms. Only after that does it read the title, caption and errors that the E2E test asserts on (the outline/render pass, &#39;VERIFY FAILED [outline] (step 1)&#39;, and the late-fault step attribution). The bootstrap inspect helper that tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs calls page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before collecting the diagnostics and screenshot behind each asserted warning. The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. So the &#39;no fixed sleeps / wait for observable state&#39; clause is unmet. This rules with Judge C. Judge A is right that the test files themselves contain no sleep calls and that the scripts poll data-step-index. That does not decide the requirement: the scripts are the browser-driving code these tests execute, they add a fixed sleep after that poll before the asserted state is read, and the integration test checks that this sleep happened. Judge B&#39;s evidence covers jsdom component tests (sample.test.tsx, presentation.test.tsx, router.test.tsx), which use waitFor/findBy and do not drive a browser. It also cites the spawnSync-based E2E test without looking at the fixed waitForTimeout inside the verify run that test drives. Clean jsdom tests cannot cancel out a browser test path that sleeps.","citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts","tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts"],"evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs:87 `await page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (SETTLE_MS = 1800 at line 17) runs before page.evaluate reads the title and caption at lines 88-98; the E2E test asserts on the outline/re…","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:67 `await page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs)` runs before collectPageDiagnostics and the screenshot at lines 68-69","tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts:34 runs the bootstrap inspect helper, lines 44-52 assert warnings from its post-sleep diagnostics, and lines 53-58 assert each capture is &gt;=1800 ms…","tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts:27-32 and 187-192 run verify.mjs and assert on render/outline outcomes it collects after the fixed sleep","A grep for &#39;settled&#39; in src/ finds no settled-state hook in the kit, so the sleep stands in for waiting on state","quoted lines: scripts/verify.mjs:15-18","quoted lines: scripts/verify.mjs:78-101","quoted lines: skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:60-72","quoted lines: tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts:33-58","quoted lines: tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts:25-37","quoted lines: tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts:181-198","decider ruling: fail, confirmed by the closed-world span audit"]}}]},"testing-evidence":null,"assumption-handling":null}

The guidance fails this criterion only when a readiness wait has no timeout. Both preview.mjs copies do give the readiness wait a timeout. waitUntilServing sets a deadline from timeoutMs (30,000 ms by default) and loops only while that deadline has not passed. It also stops early if the child process exits, and it throws a timeout error when the deadline expires. The auditor&#39;s case needs a single fetch to a loopback vite preview server to hang. Nothing in the material shows that happening. A connection to a port with no listener is refused at once, and Node&#39;s built-in fetch has its own default timeouts. So this is a hypothetical input that the review guidance does not name, and it does not defeat the pass. The other two clauses also hold. In verify and inspect, the build runs to completion through spawnSync before startPreview is called. Readiness comes from HTTP polling, and the preview&#39;s stdout is ignored, so the ready-URL parsing clause does not apply.","evidence":["In scripts/lib/preview.mjs and its template copy, waitUntilServing computes `deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs`, loops `while (Date.now() &lt; deadline)`, and throws `vite preview did not answer at $…","Each fetch is a probe to a loopback port; a refused connection rejects at once and is caught.
